Welcome to our School
A preparatory school for boys and girls aged 2-11 located in a rural village just 3 miles from Stonehenge.
We believe that every child is an individual and we aim to put the child at the heart of everything we do.
There are many reasons why so many choose to entrust Avondale with the care and development of their children. But ultimately, it comes down to our balanced approach to education and the nurturing environment we offer. At Avondale, we know that education is about so much more than academic achievement. We believe all children have a talent or a gift at which they can excel. It is very important that our curriculum offers the children the opportunity to develop skills across a wide range of subjects.

History
Where it all began...
Avondale Preparatory School was founded by Captain Perks of the Worcester Regiment and the Army Education Corps in 1923. The school site moved from Amesbury to its present location in 1957.
A Rich History
In September 2000, Richard and Susanna McNeall became joint Heads of Avondale. As the eldest daughter of Lt. Col and Mrs Holmes, the Bursar and Headmistress from 1982 to 2000, Mrs McNeall had a strong affiliation with the school. She attended Avondale as a pupil and then witnessed its development over the 18 years her parents were running the school. During this time, the house and grounds were greatly extended.
Mr Watson continued to invest in the maintenance and enhancement of school facilities over his 14 year tenure, before selling the school to Mr David Allison in 2024. The school now has a number of new EYFS teaching spaces, each supported with soft playground and covered areas. Additionally, the school now has its own adventure playground and Astroturf for wider sporting use.

About Us
Welcome to Avondale Preparatory School
Welcome to the online home of Avondale Preparatory School. Whether you are a prospective family seeking the right setting for your child, a current parent, or an educational professional exploring opportunities to join our team, I am delighted to welcome you to our website.
As the incoming Headteacher starting this September, I am thrilled to lead our vibrant school community into its next exciting chapter. Drawing on my extensive background in school leadership, my top priority is to provide steady, clear guidance and a supportive, ambitious environment where both our pupils and staff flourish.
Nestled in the heart of Wiltshire on the edge of Salisbury Plain, Avondale is a warm and distinctive independent prep school. From our youngest two-year-olds taking their first joyful steps in Nursery through to our eleven-year-olds preparing for secondary transition, we are committed to nurturing both academic excellence and strength of character. Grounded in our core values of family, integrity, community, resilience, and creativity, we provide a dependable, inspiring anchor for all our families â€” including our valued military and service community whose strength and traditions deeply enrich our school life.
We believe that an outstanding school is built on strong partnerships, visible leadership, and a shared commitment to continuous growth. I invite you to explore our website to discover our curriculum, experience our vibrant ethos, and learn more about what makes an Avondale education so unique. Whether you are seeking an exceptional educational foundation for your child or a dynamic professional environment to advance your career as an educational professional, we look forward to welcoming you.
Headteacher, Avondale Preparatory School

Aims and Ethos
Building Confidence, Strengthening Community and Inspiring Creativity.
At Avondale, we foster self-belief, promote curiosity and build resilience. We create this ethos and achieve these aims by providing a warm, happy, family atmosphere, which ensures all children are valued and cared for as individuals.
Building Confidence
Avondale is a supportive and nurturing environment, which is committed to understanding and embracing the character and strengths of each child.
“One important key to success is self-confidence. An important key to self-confidence is preparation.” -Arthur Ashe
From an early age, we encourage pupils to develop confidence, resilience and a willingness to embrace new challenges in a supportive and enriching environment. Every child is given opportunities to discover and develop their unique talents through sport, music, drama, public speaking and a wide range of extracurricular activities, helping to build self-esteem, teamwork and respect for others. Leadership is nurtured through our House system, enrichment opportunities and prefect roles, ensuring pupils grow in responsibility and leave us as confident, capable individuals ready for the next stage of their education.
Strengthening Community
From the moment your child joins Avondale, they become an important part of our vibrant school community. As an extremely welcoming family school, we ensure every child has the individual support and best possible care throughout.
“One of the marvellous things about community is that it enables us to welcome and help people in a way we couldn't as individuals.” – Jean Vanier
At Avondale, kindness, wellbeing and a strong sense of community are at the heart of everything we do. We create a warm, supportive environment where every child feels happy, safe and valued, encouraging them to be kind to others and to themselves. As a close-knit school, our staff know every pupil as an individual, enabling us to provide exceptional care and support while fostering respectful, inclusive relationships across all age groups. We believe that happy, confident children thrive both personally and academically, making Avondale more than a place of learning—it is a family.
Inspiring Creativity
Avondale aims to develop individual all-round achievement by providing a wide variety of opportunities, allowing children with varied interests to shine.
"You can't use up creativity. The more you use the more you have." - Maya Angelou

Pastoral Care
Welcome to our Home
First and foremost, Avondale is a HOME and not an institution. This, undoubtedly, has a huge impact on how children conduct themselves around the setting. We pride ourselves on providing an incredibly nurturing environment where a child’s relationship with their teacher is key. The size of our classrooms and number of children in respective year groups ensures an intimate education experience, where children feel confident in voicing their ideas. We operate an open- door policy where communication between home and school is encouraged. Likewise, we share areas of strength and anything requiring remedial attention as things surface.
Positive Mental Health
At Avondale Preparatory School, we are committed to supporting the emotional health and wellbeing of our pupils and staff. We have a caring ethos, where each individual is valued.
At our school, we know that everyone experiences life challenges that can make us vulnerable and at times, anyone may need additional emotional support. We take the view that positive mental health is everybody’s business and that we all have a role to play.
We take a whole school approach to promoting positive mental health that aims to help pupils become more resilient, be happy and successful and prevent problems before they arise.
We also recognise the role that stigma can play in preventing understanding and awareness of mental health issues and aim to create an open and positive culture that encourages discussion and understanding of mental health issues. We aim to be a ‘talking school’ with an ‘Open Door Policy’.
Should you wish to seek support elsewhere, please find below a selection of websites and organisations that can offer guidance in how to best support mental health and well-being.

pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Care
Our Morning Welcome
The Avondale school day begins at 8am each morning, but there is a Before School Care Club from 7:30AM to support our parents.
Part of Avondale’s character is borne out of the way our older children support the younger ones; in this respect all children play outside together in the mornings until registration at 8:30am.
After School Care
Nursery and Tots, officially finish at 3pm for those accessing Free Entitlement Funding. Children staying on, are provided for in our After School Care Club, which sees our older children join at 3:20pm, when their school day finishes.
After School Care Club is charged at £4 per half hour, or part thereof (one hour minimum). There is a 5% discount on fees for families with two children and a 20% discount on fees for families with three children.
ASCC runs until 5.30pm daily. The children are given a substantial afternoon tea, and enjoy outdoor play, indoor games, art activities and computer games. Some of the older children also have the opportunity to start their home learning or participate in teacher- led clubs ranging from sports to choir. Whilst teacher- led clubs are charged at the same rate as the ASCC, we wish to develop further our school sporting teams and choir performances- subsequently, these clubs are free of charge. The clubs available, the age group involved and the days the clubs take place are dependent on staffing – details of these are sent out each term in our calendar.
Please be aware that sports activities are weather dependent and may need to be cancelled in the event of bad weather – if necessary, please telephone after 2pm to check if clubs are running. We shall do our best to communicate with you via text message.

Curriculum
Our aim at every stage is to provide a nurturing and encouraging learning environment for our pupils; one where they are challenged to reach their potential in every subject, and given support in any areas that they struggle with.
Bringing the curriculum to life is one of the challenges we relish. Our aim is to develop pupils’ ability to learn through the explicit teaching of effective learning habits and skills. We encourage pupils to be inquisitive, engaged, resilient and organised learners who are well prepared for the academic challenges they will face.
We have designed our curriculum to ignite excitement and form meaningful cross-curricular links between subjects, allowing more time for exploring and mastering topics and encouraging pupils to develop a passion and interest in particular areas.

Fee Notes & Policies
Nursery Fees: Termly basis, payable on the first day of term. Late payments incur £5 per day.
Invoices emailed at least one week before term, include fees in advance, other charges, and outstanding balances.
School may use deposit to settle any outstanding debts if parents leave without notice.
Nursery Declarations:
Parents must confirm desired learning sessions with Mrs. Lister before term starts.
Termly invoices reflect this declaration.
Priority: full-time children first, then first-come, first-served.
Hour increases subject to availability; billed monthly.
Consent form for funding code must be completed before term starts; otherwise full fees apply.
Withdrawal: Full term’s written notice required. Without notice, full term’s fees are payable. No refunds for disciplinary or voluntary withdrawals.
Additional Costs: Financial support may be available for families struggling to cover costs above free entitlement hours.
Consumables: Parents provide essential items (nappies, wipes, sun cream, etc.); list provided upon enrolment

Avondale has very active and supportive Parent-Teacher Association (PTA). The PTA work to enhance the pupils' experience at the school and bring the wider community together.
They arrange regular events for parents and children to socialise, as well as raising funds to support school projects which benefit the pupils. Everyone is warmly invited to attend all of these events, whether as an active participant or simply to meet other parents and learn more.
The PTA organisation includes specific roles such as Chair, Secretary and Treasurer. We welcome anyone who is interested in helping. Please get in touch via email with Emma Hillyard on PTA@avondaleschool.org.

Reception Class
At this level, there is a mix of adult-led or child-initiated activities and much of the curriculum is built from the children’s interests. Our ethos strongly builds upon learning through play, learning through the environment and learning through meaningful and engaging experiences. We believe these are the key elements that build the foundations for a lifelong love of learning.
We spend lots of time focusing on the Characteristics of Effective Learning where we support children to become confident, independent and resilient learners. We always empower our children to believe everything is possible.
An Exciting Place to Learn
Reception benefits from a sheltered decking area as well as a wonderful outdoor space which is solely used by Reception children. Children are able to access the outdoor spaces on a free-flow basis, daily. Phonics becomes a significant focus within the Reception year. We use ‘Cued Articulation’ alongside our phonics curriculum, which helps children’s speaking skills as well as their reading and writing skills. This has proved extremely successful.
The children take part in weekly cooking, art and library sessions; enjoying and borrowing books from our own school library. The children also enjoy P.E at least once a week and are taught music and French by specialist teachers.
Communicating with Parents
We use Tapestry which is an online learning journal. Parents are able to view their child’s learning, progress and next steps, as well as how much fun the children are having at school, whilst also uploading their own comments and media. A strong link is built between school and home. Parents are updated weekly on their children’s learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Avondale Prep School - The Arts at Avondale
pageCache.text:
The Arts at Avondale
We believe every child has their own creative spark and during their time at Avondale, we'll uncover and nurture this talent. Whether it’s through art, music or drama, we use the arts to enable our pupils to express themselves and enjoy the freedom to be creative.
Each department has a specialised teacher with great enthusiasm and passion within their specific subject. The music department also offers additional lessons with extra staff for a wide variety of instruments.
Art & Design
We believe every child is an artist and our aim is to build confidence through creative play and visual self-expression so as to allow their potential to flourish.
Pupils who are keen to develop their talents further in these subjects have access to numerous clubs after school.
Music
Music plays a crucial role at Avondale, from the moment pupils enter Nursery they are given plenty of opportunities to develop their talents. Pupils at Avondale receive a weekly Music lesson taught by a specialist Music teacher and are encouraged to sing in a choir, learn an instrument or play a role in the extra-curricular life of the school.
Singing is fundamental to every Music lesson and our pupils are taught a diverse and engaging repertoire. The opportunity children have to make and perform music is a real strength of the Department. Pupils are given regular opportunities to perform in concerts, as soloists or as part of ensembles. This enables children to gain confidence in front of an audience; we pride ourselves on the quality of these performances and the pupils relish the opportunities to perform.
Drama
Drama at Avondale is a vibrant and central aspect of the school curriculum, and plays an integral role in the personal development of the children.
With an exciting curriculum and regular performance opportunities, our pupils are able to improve their speaking and social skills in an engaging and safe learning environment.

pageCache.pageTitle: Avondale Prep School - Tots and Nursery
pageCache.text:
Tots and Nursery
Our Tots and Nursery classes cater for children aged two to school age, during school term times. We operate from 8am to 5:30pm and offer a range of sessions spanning these hours. We provide a hot, nutritious lunch, along with a variety of healthy snacks and a light afternoon tea. We have a compulsory school uniform which allows us to feel part of the wider school community.
Outdoor & Physical Learning
We operate out of two learning spaces, fully equipped to provide high quality experiences and learning across all areas of development. Our newly installed grassed spaces, along with our large playing field, adventure playground and Astro turf court area, provide ample opportunity for outdoor and physical learning; we also have a further hard-court playground where we can be often found whizzing around on our bicycles, trikes and cars. We are fortunate in being able to join the rest of the school for many events, including singing with our fantastic music teacher and attending celebration assemblies.
Child Centred Learning
Our approach to learning is child centred and focuses on the interests and needs of the children, with a large portion of our learning being child initiated. We recognise that children learn and develop well in environments that enable role play and physical activity; progress is made with encouragement from experienced and familiar adults who know and respond to every child's individuality. We understand that every child is unique and we strive to provide the best start for all children. We are extremely proud of how our children develop and flourish during their time in our care
High Quality Care
Along with high quality learning experiences, we also strive to offer high quality care. We focus on building strong relationships with your children and place emphasis on supporting children’s emotional well-being. We have space where children can sleep and rest (should they need to), and there is always an adult on hand for a cuddle or a bit of reassurance when required.
